pairs: I turned myself to other things,
et vidi calumnias quæ sub sole geruntur,
and I saw the false accusations which are carried out under the sun,
and the tears of the innocent,
and that there was no one to console them;
and that they were not able to withstand their violence,
et laudavi magis mortuos quam viventes;
And so, I praised the dead more than the living.
et feliciorem utroque judicavi qui necdum natus est,
And happier than both of these, I judged him to be, who has not yet been born,
nec vidit mala quæ sub sole fiunt.
and who has not yet seen the evils which are done under the sun.
Rursum contemplatus sum omnes labores hominum,
Again, I was contemplating all the labors of men.
et industrias animadverti patere invidiæ proximi;
And I took notice that their endeavors are open to the envy of their neighbor. And so,
et in hoc ergo vanitas et cura superflua est.
in this, too, there is emptiness and superfluous anxiety.
The foolish man folds his hands together,
and he consumes his own flesh,
“A handful with rest is better than both hands filled with labors
quam plena utraque manus cum labore et afflictione animi.
and with affliction of the soul.”
reperi et aliam vanitatem sub sole.
I also discovered another vanity under the sun.
and he does not have a second:
And yet he does not cease to labor,
nor are his eyes satisfied with wealth,
“For whom do I labor and cheat my soul of good things?”
is emptiness and a most burdensome affliction.
Melius est ergo duos esse simul quam unum;
Therefore, it is better for two to be together, than for one to be alone.
For they have the advantage of their companionship.
he shall be supported by the other.
Woe to one who is alone.
he has no one to lift him up.
How can one person alone be warmed?
Et si quispiam prævaluerit contra unum,
And if a man can prevail against one,
and a threefold cord is broken with difficulty.
who does not know to look ahead for the sake of posterity.
Quod de carcere catenisque interdum quis egrediatur ad regnum;
For sometimes, one goes forth from prison and chains, to a kingdom,
Vidi cunctos viventes qui ambulant sub sole cum adolescente secundo,
I saw all the living who are walking under the sun, and I saw the next generation,
who shall rise up in their places.
Infinitus numerus est populi omnium qui fuerunt ante eum,
The number of people, out of all who existed before these, is boundless.
et qui postea futuri sunt non lætabuntur in eo;
And those who will exist afterwards shall not rejoice in them.
sed et hoc vanitas et afflictio spiritus.
But this, too, is emptiness and an affliction of the spirit.
Custodi pedem tuum ingrediens domum Dei,
Guard your foot, when you step into the house of God,
and draw near, so that you may listen.
Multo enim melior est obedientia quam stultorum victimæ,
For obedience is much better than the sacrifices of the foolish,
who do not know the evil that they are doing.
